questions.question: build.html: 1 font sizes sit within 2px of a neighbour (14). Are those distinct steps or the same intent typed twice?
questions.answer: Distinct roles, not distinct steps — so: the same intent typed more than once. 13px is .foot; 14px is .idea .hook, .pocket .x and .empty. Each size is attached to a different element, which is why they exist. But 13 → 14 (7.7%) at body-copy size is under ~8% change, and a type step is not legible below roughly 15%; on build.html they render as one size with extra decimals. Collapse to 14px for all four. questions.question: 35 rendered card(s) exist. Open the most recent: does the artwork breathe, or is it crowded by the frame? Nothing in source can answer that.
questions.answer: NEITHER — there was no artwork to breathe. Opened research/pulse/cards/latest-social.png and the entire left half was an empty rounded rectangle where the product photo belongs. Cause: the card SVGs carry a REMOTE href (tcgplayer-cdn.tcgplayer.com), a rasteriser cannot fetch over the network, and scripts/rasterize-cards.mjs — which fetches and base64-embeds each image before rasterising — was in NO workflow at all. So cards were minted as SVG every day and never re-rasterised, and every committed PNG was stale. Verified: 0 of the card SVGs hold an embedded data: image; all hold remote hrefs. Running the rasteriser took latest-social.png from 42KB to 542KB and the product now renders. Now wired into the pipeline as step 16. On the original question: with the image present the layout does breathe — image left, stack right, and the wordmark is NOT clipped (checked at full resolution after a downscaled view suggested it was; it has 12px of clearance).

questions.question: Does PPT document a window for ebaySold, or accept a period parameter? A baseline snapshot is in data/graded-window-probe.json - an all-time count can only grow, so a count that DROPS a week later proves a rolling window and unblocks every graded figure we withdrew.
questions.answer: PARTLY ANSWERED ALREADY, and the answer is more awkward than yes or no — see research/reports/2026-08-23-namespace-verified.md, Block 2. PPT does NOT document a window and accepts no period parameter, but the data carries dates: every graded card has ebay.dateRangeStart/dateRangeEnd, and 99% of per-grade rows carry lastSaleDate. THE TRAP: the block-level range does NOT describe the per-grade aggregates. Measured across 309 graded cards and 2,669 grade rows, 21% have a lastSaleDate OUTSIDE the block's stated range — one example shows a cgc9 median resting on sales whose most recent is eight months before the window printed above it. So labelling a graded price with dateRangeStart would mislabel one in five. A defensible per-grade window DOES exist in smartMarketPrice.daysUsed plus confidence, on the 582 rows (22%) at medium or high confidence. The baseline probe in data/graded-window-probe.json is still the right definitive test for rolling-vs-all-time and should be re-read on schedule.

questions.question: faq.html: 1 font sizes sit within 2px of a neighbour (16). Are those distinct steps or the same intent typed twice?
questions.answer: A FINDING ABOUT THE CHECK, not the page. faq.html now uses 14px supporting and 16px body — 2px apart, so this still flags, but 14 to 16 is a 14.3% step and that DOES read as a step. The pairs I called noise elsewhere (13 to 14, 14 to 14.5) are 3-8%. The threshold is absolute where it should be proportional: 2px is a large step at 12px and an invisible one at 30px. Suggest the check flags a gap under roughly 12% of the smaller size instead of under 2px. I set this page to 14/16 deliberately and am leaving it — it is correct typographically and will keep tripping an absolute rule until the rule is proportional.

questions.question: Does a want-list image actually read well at Discord thumbnail size? Nine cards plus prices plus a total is a lot in a 400px preview, and that is where a trade list is usually seen first.
questions.answer: TESTED, and the answer is half. Rendered a nine-card image and downscaled it to 400px — the ARTWORK survives: every card is identifiable, the colours carry, and the caption line is legible. The fine text does not. The want-list price font is 26px on a 2535px canvas, which is 4.1px at 400px wide — illegible, as are the year labels and the illustrator credit. So a nine-card want list reads at thumbnail size as 'nine cards' and not as 'which ones I need and what they cost', which is the working half of a working document. Recommend want/trade/sell intent caps at 4-6 cards, or scales the price text with card count rather than holding it at 26px. Verified by eye at 400px, not inferred.
